How to read this

  • Difference is after-minus-before win rate in percentage points. Filters pool all matching encounter profiles equally; the selected category and target-count filters let you isolate matchup types.
  • Eligibility means the character has a qualifying trigger under the simulator’s current ability definitions. Trigger counts show average activations per battle. Dark Matter activates on a damaging Basic Attack, Skill, or Ultimate and then cools down for two wearer turns. Clear Skies stacks a new shield after each skill.
  • Baseline and after runs use the same level-one party, level-one Runes, weapons, encounter, and starting conditions. Only the one wearer’s set effect changes. Parties are Soul/Lily/Dawn/Logan and Soul/Zero/Dawn/Logan.
  • Short enemy HP is 0.65×. Medium HP is 3× for Common/Elite and 5× for Boss; Long HP is 8×. Difficulty scales enemy attack by category (Common 5×/10×/20×; Elite 1×/1.5×/2.5×; Boss 0.2×/0.3×/0.46×) and defense by 0.85×/1×/1.2×. These factors were calibrated against the level-one parties so easy through hard profiles produce useful win-rate ranges.
  • United eligibility follows the current simulator’s ally-target rule: Dawn and Logan qualify; Soul’s self-only Enhance is treated as not targeting an ally. Eternal Sun requires a damaging Ultimate, so Dawn is ineligible.
  • Effects use your latest proposed values: Radiant Moon gives 50% Echo on damaging Skills and has a two-turn cooldown; Eternal Sun guarantees the next damaging Ultimate crit with +50 percentage points of Critical Damage, then has a two-turn cooldown; Celestial Star advances 100% with a two-turn cooldown; Dark Matter ignores both defenses by 25% and boosts physical/magical/true damage by 25% on an eligible attack action, then cools down for two wearer turns; Clear Skies adds a 10%-Max-HP shield after each skill, lasting two wearer turns; shield layers stack, and reflect increases by 10 percentage points while shielded; Infinite Space delays all living enemies by 100% and cannot affect each enemy again for two of that enemy’s turns; Recycle restores one Skill Point and 20 Energy, then cools down for the wearer’s next two turns; Amplify boosts the full Basic Attack action by 50% and cools down for the wearer’s next two turns; United advances the wearer 50% and restores 20 Energy after an ally-targeted Skill, then cools down for the next two wearer turns.
  • Each exact condition has 150 simulations. Narrow filters therefore have more sampling noise than the pooled comparison; small win-rate differences may not be reliable.
